title: Black Family Wealth Fell 25% While America's Rose: The Fed Data | Across the Water, Ep. 14
lede: The Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances found that the median Black family's net worth fell 25% between 2022 and 2025, after inflation, from $49,100 to $36,800, while the median for all families rose 2%. Black families were the only group whose median fell, and the White-to-Black wealth ratio reached about nine to one, the widest since 2016. This episode explains the data, the 2019–2022 surge that came before, what families own, the explanations researchers offer and what to watch.
keyPoints: Median Black family net worth fell 25% from 2022 to 2025, to $36,800 (2025 dollars); White +6%, Hispanic +18%, Asian +16%, all families +2% (Federal Reserve, SCF 2025).
The White median was about nine times the Black median in 2025, the largest ratio since 2016 (Federal Reserve).
Black median wealth had risen 60% from 2019 to 2022, the fastest of any group (Federal Reserve, SCF 2022).
One in three Black families has a retirement account, against 63% of White families; median stock holdings of stock owners rose 36% (Federal Reserve; Tax Policy Center via The Community Voice).
60% of Black adults said they were doing at least okay financially in 2025, down 5 points (Federal Reserve, SHED).
